paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Laodicea looked at itself and said, "I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing" (Revelation 3:17). Jesus looked at the same church and saw them as "wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked" (Revelation 3:17). The most dangerous place to be is thinking you've got it all together when you don't.

Now here's the part that gets me. Jesus doesn't walk away. He says, "Those I love I rebuke and discipline" (Revelation 3:19). The hard words come with a call to be earnest and repent (Revelation 3:19), and the fix is real: gold, white garments and salve, all offered by Him (Revelation 3:18).

And then LISTEN to this: Jesus says, "Behold, I stand at the door and knock" (Revelation 3:20). If anyone hears His voice and opens the door, He will come in and dine with them (Revelation 3:20). He isn't just correcting, He's inviting you to the table, and He promises the one who overcomes a seat with Him on His throne (Revelation 3:21). That's the last letter of the seven, and the Spirit's word to every church is to listen (Revelation 3:22).
